I think a related fact is that technological change is often a response to marginal living conditions. When your people are starving, a successful society figures out a way to produce enough food for them (agriculture). It figures out how to defend them from other tribes looking to take that food (metallurgy). Once these fundamentals are in place, a society may or may not go on to further industrialization, but it's not going to get there without them.

Add that being unhappy is (unfortunately) a positive survival trait. It doesn't pay to be morosely depressed, of course, but being dissatisfied with the current situation is a driver of change. It may well be that the more marginal the conditions, the more the dissatisfied disposition has an advantage over the happy one.

This is not to say there isn't a survival advantage to high tech in equatorial regions. Certainly malaria alone constitutes a major threat to survival. It's just that the technology required to deal with it is enough steps down the chain that it never gets off the ground, because there is no survival advantage to the intermediate steps.
